fixer.title: Keep idle sash gripper styling from restyling the whole workbench

introducer.title: workbench: auto-hide sash grippers when the mouse is idle

cases.mechanism: Frequently toggling inherited CSS custom properties on the workbench root invalidated computed style for every descendant and forced large synchronous browser style recalculations on mouse activity and idle transitions.
cases.symptom: With large chat/session DOMs, showing or hiding sash grippers blocked the renderer main thread for roughly 0.4 seconds per transition and materially delayed session switching.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added descendant selector at style.css:70 places the custom properties directly on `.monaco-sash` descendants. Root class toggles now invalidate and recompute only sash elements while preserving inheritance to each sash pseudo-element, as covered by the added computed-style test and existing gripper transition tests.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, style.css:69 assigns two inherited custom properties on `.monaco-workbench.sash-grippers-hidden`. `SashGrippersController.registerContainer` removes that root class on mouse movement and re-adds it after the idle timer (sash.ts:103-109), so each idle/active transition invalidates inherited style across the entire workbench even though searches show the properties are consumed only by sash `::after` rules in sashHandles.css and sessions workbench.css. The PR's measured scenario reports synchronous 393-400 ms style recalculations over about 34,300 elements during these toggles. Blame identifies f5d95e4ba024c912a62793b3167eeb119fb150dc as introducing the base selector.
